overview: Myanmar, also called Burma, is a country in South-East Asia. Its capital is Naypyidaw, while Yangon is its largest city. Myanmar became independent from the United Kingdom in 1948. The military seized power in a coup in 2021, which led to widespread conflict. Most people are Buddhist, and the country is famous for golden pagodas such as Shwedagon.

geography.text: Myanmar is shaped by mountains that run from north to south, with the Himalayas reaching into the far north. The Irrawaddy river flows down the middle of the country to a large delta on the Andaman Sea, where much of its rice is grown. A long, narrow strip of the country runs south along the coast towards Thailand.

history.text: From the 1000s the kingdom of Bagan built thousands of Buddhist temples on the plains of central Myanmar. Britain conquered the country in three wars in the 1800s and ruled it as part of British India. Burma became independent in 1948. The military ruled for most of the time after 1962, and after a short period of civilian government it seized power again in 2021.

events.title: Bagan kingdom
events.text: King Anawrahta founds the first Burmese empire.

events.title: British conquest
events.text: Britain completes its conquest of Burma.

events.title: Nobel Peace Prize
events.text: Aung San Suu Kyi wins the prize while under house arrest.

events.title: Coup
events.text: The military overthrows the elected government.

government.text: Myanmar has been ruled by the military since a coup in February 2021 removed the elected government of Aung San Suu Kyi's National League for Democracy. Since then a civil war has spread across the country, with many armed groups fighting the army. The army held a widely criticised election in 2025.

economy.text: Myanmar is one of the poorest countries in Asia. It exports natural gas, rice, clothing, jade and rare-earth minerals. The coup and civil war have caused the economy to shrink sharply.

culture.text: Myanmar is a mostly Buddhist country with thousands of golden temples and pagodas. The Shwedagon Pagoda in Yangon is covered in gold. Many people wear a longyi, a long sarong, and apply thanaka, a yellow paste made from tree bark, to their faces.

items.title: Shwedagon Pagoda
items.text: A gold-covered stupa about 100 metres tall.

items.title: Bagan
items.text: More than 2,000 temples on a plain, listed by UNESCO.

items.title: Thanaka
items.text: A paste worn on the face as sunscreen and make-up.

sport.text: Football is very popular, and chinlone, in which a team keeps a rattan ball in the air with their feet, is a traditional sport. Lethwei, a fierce form of kickboxing that allows head-butts, is also traditional.

items.title: Chinlone
items.text: A team game without opponents, mixing sport and dance.
